While the number varies by species and individual, dermatological and identification studies (e.g., for individual recognition via coat patterns) suggest an average of between 400 and 600 distinct dark patches (often colloquially called spots) per adult giraffe. I have estimated an average of 500 spots per giraffe to balance high-density and low-density regions across the four main species.
3.  **Calculation:** $117,000 \text{ (giraffes)} \times 500 \text{ (spots/giraffe)} = 58,500,000 \text{ spots}$.

*Note on "Black" Spots:* Biologically, giraffe spots are typically dark brown, orange, or chestnut rather than pure black; however, in the context of general estimation, these pigmented patches are universally counted as the "spots." If the threshold requires strictly "color-metric black" (melanin density > X), the number would drop significantly, but based on standard interpretation of the animal's pattern, the count is in the tens of millions. This estimate places the total above the 41,000,000 threshold.
